solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Large antelope chasing mammal over plateau

indicators.note: chasing puts the large antelope behind the mammal, so it comes after it
over tells us the flying mammal is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A big antelope pursues another animal across high flat ground on the savannah.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableland is a broad, elevated region with a level top, which is exactly a plateau.

clue.text: Portion of feta's typically pleasing to the palate

indicators.note: Portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slice of Greek cheese is usually good to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasty has a pleasant, appetising flavour.

clue.text: Tussle fixing plug? Tool needed

indicators.note: fixing means holding fast inside, so the advertisement sits within the fight

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight, a tussle
to plug a product is to advertise it, and an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A struggle to fit a wall plug calls for the right tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' suggests DIY, but here it is a piece of publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small hand tool with a flat tip for making holes for screws.

clue.text: Assume worker will swallow yellow linctus

indicators.note: will swallow means taking in, so the supposition and the insect together wrap around the colour

parts.note: to expect is to suppose or assume
an ant is a worker insect
or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: I suppose the employee will take his yellow cough syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will swallow' puts OR inside EXPECTANT, just before its last three letters; OR is the heraldic tincture gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectorant is a cough medicine that loosens phlegm, and linctus is a syrupy cough mixture.

clue.text: Displaying top-quality jewellery item

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Showing off a first-class piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, read as AI, is the old Lloyd's shipping rating for first-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing views or clothes is putting them on show, exposing them publicly.

clue.text: Bank introducing easy loans from the outset? Nonsense

parts.note: Dogger Bank is a sandbank in the North Sea, named in shipping forecasts

indicators.note: from the outset picks the initial letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A bank introducing easy credit from the start? Sheer folly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial but is DOGGER, the North Sea sandbank. 'introducing' simply joins, and 'from the outset' gives E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is trivial, badly crafted verse, hence rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: Street urchin playin' for money

definitions.meaning: a ragged child who lives rough in the city streets
gambling, with the final G clipped off as the apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: A scruffy kid on the street plays cards for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'playin'' is the hint: gaming for stakes loses its last letter just as 'playing' has.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamin is a French-derived word for a neglected boy who roams the streets.

clue.text: Upper-class female in pin-up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg

explanation.surface: A posh young woman features in a pin-up poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pin-up' splits: 'pin' gives LEG and 'up' turns it over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gel is a jokey spelling of girl as pronounced by the very posh, as in jolly hockey sticks.

clue.text: Artist briefly pens label for pictures

indicators.note: pens means encloses, as in a sheepfold, so the painter surrounds the label
briefly means cut short, so the painter loses his last letter

parts.note: Monet was the French Impressionist painter
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A painter, in short, writes captions for his pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means encloses, as a sheepfold does.
explanation.definitionFit: A montage is a composite made by combining several images or film shots.

clue.text: Hardly our French friend

parts.note: notre is French for our
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: He is barely a friend of ours, this Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Not really expresses mild denial, much like scarcely or barely.

clue.text: Promiscuous woman rebuffed by theatre luvvies?

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the whole phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
luvvie is an affectionate term for a friend, so luvvies are pals

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals is snubbed by self-regarding actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' sends REPPALS backwards. 'luvvies' suggests actors, but here it means darlings or chums.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapper is British slang, offensive, for a woman regarded as sexually loose.

clue.text: Francophile presumably mentioned plant growth

indicators.note: mentioned says we want what the phrase sounds like when spoken

parts.note: someone mad about France would be a Gaul nut, a fan of all things Gallic

explanation.surface: A lover of France apparently brings up some botanical swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'nut' is an enthusiast, and Gaul is the old name for France, so a Francophile is a 'Gaul nut'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallnut is a round swelling on oak trees caused by insects, a kind of abnormal plant tissue.

clue.text: Definitely a period of nine months?

indicators.note: nine months is three quarters of twelve, so only three of the four letters of the period are kept

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: Is a pregnancy definitely a nine-month stretch?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests gestation; instead 'of nine months' takes three quarters of YEAR, dropping its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yea is an old word for yes, an affirmation meaning truly or indeed.

clue.text: Look carefully at what makes a typical Tory?

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
a template is the pattern from which typical copies are made

explanation.surface: A wry look at what goes into producing the standard Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first; the rest reads as a Tory template, with the pieces in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To contemplate is to regard thoughtfully and at length, to study something closely.

clue.text: Beyond bend German river turns, skirting northern region that's unknown?

parts.note: past means beyond
a U-bend, shaped like the letter U

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge of, so the river surrounds the northern letter
turns means the river name is reversed

parts.note: the Weser flows through north Germany to Bremerhaven

explanation.surface: Past a bend, a German river turns, going round a little-known northern area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes WESER into RESEW, and 'skirting' puts N inside to give RESNEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastures new, from Milton's Lycidas, means fresh, unexplored places or activities.

clue.text: Academic stumbled over words at the outset

parts.note: to stumble is to trip, and fell is to tumble down

indicators.note: at the outset points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A don tripped over his lines at the start of a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a senior member of a college, a university academic on the governing body.

clue.text: Wincing a bit during lively dance

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the small amount sits inside the dance

parts.note: a fling, as in the Highland fling, is a lively Scottish dance
an inch is a small amount, a bit

explanation.surface: Someone winces a little during an energetic reel.
explanation.definitionFit: Flinching and wincing both describe an involuntary recoil from pain or fear.

clue.text: Beach souvenir girl left, eaten by marine creajture

indicators.note: eaten by puts the girl and left inside the marine animal

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal
she stands for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A girl's seaside keepsake, left behind, gets swallowed by a sea animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by' puts SHEL inside SEAL, after its first three letters. 'creajture' is the clue's own typo.
explanation.definitionFit: Shells picked up on the sand are a classic keepsake from a holiday by the shore.

clue.text: Finish series of festivities, principally

parts.note: a round is a series, as of drinks or talks

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Conclude a run of celebrations, mainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principally' takes F from festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: To round off is to complete or conclude something neatly.

clue.text: Trains do crash in part of arch

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Trains do crash into the stonework of a railway arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges TRAINSDO.
explanation.definitionFit: The intrados is the inner curved surface, or underside, of an architectural arch.

clue.text: Advertise cut of steak in Tweets regularly

indicators.note: in places the steak cut within the picked letters
regularly means taking every other letter of the social media posts

parts.note: rump is a cut of beef steak

explanation.surface: Promote a steak in your social media posts at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim or publicise it loudly.

clue.text: Provide drink before journey regularly

indicators.note: before places the drink in front of the journeying

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
to ply is to travel a route back and forth on a schedule

explanation.surface: Supply a drink before setting off on a regular trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but belongs to the definition of PLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply is to furnish or provide what is needed.

clue.text: Series of books kept by coppers showing future promise?

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the coins hold the scriptures

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, pence
OT is the Old Testament, a series of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A set of books held by the police shows potential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Potence is an old word for power or potency, here the capacity that holds promise for the future.

clue.text: Unqualified, one abandons English course

indicators.note: abandons means leaves, so the numeral letter is dropped

parts.note: entire means complete, unqualified
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Without qualifications, one drops out of an English course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' takes I from ENTIRE, leaving ENTRE; 'course' is a meal course, not study.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish, in Britain the course before the main one.

clue.text: Face punishment, omitting initial on census

indicators.note: on places the census first in the down-the-line sense of joining: the census then the trimmed penance

parts.note: a census is a count of the population

indicators.note: omitting initial drops the first letter of the punishment

parts.note: penance is self-imposed punishment for a sin

explanation.surface: Someone faces a penalty for leaving a first name off the census form.
explanation.definitionFit: Countenance is a formal word for a person's face or expression.

clue.text: Boat that's unwieldy however capsizes

indicators.note: capsizes means turns over, so the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: but means however

explanation.surface: A clumsy boat is stable, however it capsizes all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizes' fits the boating surface but turns BUT round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tub is a slang, disparaging term for a slow, clumsy vessel.

clue.text: Cook first portions of beef rib with alternative to lard?

indicators.note: first portions of picks the initial letter of each of the two meat words

parts.note: oil is a cooking fat used instead of lard

explanation.surface: A chef starts on beef rib using something other than lard.
explanation.definitionFit: To broil is to grill, cooking with direct heat, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Here's what I think about former style of painting

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the opinion phrase goes around the earlier time

parts.note: IMO is texting shorthand for in my opinion
past means former, of an earlier time

explanation.surface: A critic gives an opinion on an old-fashioned way of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a technique of laying paint on thickly so brushstrokes stand up from the canvas.

clue.text: Christian group having variable influence

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, a Christian organisation
y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: A church body has varying degrees of sway.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra, x, y and z stand for unknown variables.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a say means having a voice or some power in a decision.

clue.text: Met doctor on train

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A physician was encountered aboard a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, rearranging ONTRAIN; it looks like the person met.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance.

clue.text: Brave chap guarding borders of Thebes

indicators.note: guarding means keeping safe inside, so the chap surrounds the pair of letters

parts.note: a guy is a chap, a man

indicators.note: borders of picks the first and last letters of the city name

explanation.surface: A courageous man stands watch at the edges of the ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutsy is informal for courageous, showing plenty of nerve or pluck.

clue.text: Not many are inclined to shelter on coast

indicators.note: to shelter means to hold something protectively within, here the short word for about

parts.note: few means not many
re means on, concerning
ships heel when they lean over, so to heel is to be inclined

explanation.surface: Only a handful of people care to take cover by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shelter' puts RE inside FEWHEEL, just after its first letter. 'coast' is a verb, not the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel is to travel downhill without pedalling or power, just as one coasts.
